title: Pongola glaciation
summary: Shales and diamictites of the Pongola Supergroup on South Africa's Kaapvaal Craton are reported to record the oldest surface glaciation known. Oxygen-isotope data from Mozaan Group shales indicate gradual cooling culminating in glacial conditions at about 2.90 billion years ago, possibly at a near-polar position; a news release describes fossilized moraines beneath the world's largest gold deposits.

uncertainty.note: Hofmann and Bindeman date the Delfkom Formation diamictites between 2.90 and 2.87 Ga and glacial conditions at ~2.90 Ga. Years are Ga counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

where.modern_name: Pongola Supergroup, Kaapvaal Craton, South Africa (pin is the Wikidata point for the craton)
where.historical_name: Kaapvaal Craton, southern Africa; no polities

paleo.not_applicable: Age is beyond the 1000 Ma limit of the MERDITH2021 plate model.

importance.justification: Reported as the oldest glaciation on record, an early test of how cold the Archaean climate could get.
